title: Expose the future-information floor and its physical locality interface
statement: A finite calibration can see the same zero-gauge channel for all hidden sign completions, while later gauge change exposes different logical rotations. Even a collective frozen full-CPTP receiver then has a source completion with order min(1,q tau^2) excess. Separately, integrated incident local interaction norms supply tau_i<=2g_i; they do not certify unknown physical couplings from the fit.

body: The approximation tube and contrasts are structural promises, not finite-data membership certificates. The bound is uniform in future memory while axes stay in the same persistent tube; arbitrary drift is excluded. It does not reconstruct a full encoding, supply a gauge spectral floor, establish redundant-code recovery or turn operator proximity into a local-stochastic threshold. Optional twirling and implementation discrepancies retain complete service scope. Read the exact supporting statement and its applicable conditions.
